requirements.quote:
For "https" resources, connection reuse additionally depends on
   having a certificate that is valid for the host in the URI.  The
   certificate presented by the server MUST satisfy any checks that the
   client would perform when forming a new TLS connection for the host
   in the URI.
requirements.condition: When reusing a connection for an "https" resource.
requirements.required_behavior: The server certificate must be valid for the URI host and satisfy every certificate check the client would perform for a new TLS connection to that host.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not reuse the connection when the certificate would fail a check applied to a new TLS connection for the URI host.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare certificate validation outcomes for connection reuse and a new TLS connection to the same URI host.

requirements.quote:
A server that does not wish clients to reuse connections can indicate
   that it is not authoritative for a request by sending a 421
   (Misdirected Request) status code in response to the request (see
   Section 15.5.20 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: When a server does not wish a client to reuse a connection for a request and elects to indicate that it is not authoritative.
requirements.required_behavior: The server sends a 421 (Misdirected Request) response to that request.
requirements.why_checkable: A response test can verify that the server uses status code 421 for this indication.

requirements.quote:
A client that is configured to use a proxy over HTTP/2 directs
   requests to that proxy through a single connection.  That is, all
   requests sent via a proxy reuse the connection to the proxy.
requirements.condition: When a client is configured to use a proxy over HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must direct all requests sent via the proxy through one connection to the proxy and reuse that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection instrumentation can verify that all proxied requests use the same proxy connection.

requirements.quote:
Implementations of HTTP/2 MUST use TLS version 1.2 [TLS12] or higher
   for HTTP/2 over TLS.
requirements.condition: When HTTP/2 is used over TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must use TLS version 1.2 or higher.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not use a TLS version lower than 1.2 for HTTP/2.
requirements.why_checkable: A negotiated HTTP/2 TLS connection exposes the selected TLS version for comparison with the minimum.

requirements.quote:
for HTTP/2 over TLS.  The general TLS usage guidance in [TLSBCP]
   SHOULD be followed, with some additional restrictions that are
   specific to HTTP/2.
requirements.condition: When implementing HTTP/2 over TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: The general TLS usage guidance in TLSBCP should be followed.
requirements.why_checkable: The referenced guidance is not present in this chunk, so the concrete implementation checkpoints cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

requirements.quote:
The TLS implementation MUST support the Server Name Indication (SNI)
   [TLS-EXT] extension to TLS.
requirements.condition: For the TLS implementation used with HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: The TLS implementation must support the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension.
requirements.why_checkable: TLS capability tests can determine whether SNI is supported.

requirements.quote:
[TLS-EXT] extension to TLS.  If the server is identified by a domain
   name [DNS-TERMS], clients MUST send the server_name TLS extension
   unless an alternative mechanism to indicate the target host is used.
requirements.condition: When a client connects to a server identified by a domain name and no alternative mechanism indicates the target host.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must send the server_name TLS extension.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not omit server_name unless an alternative target-host indication mechanism is used.
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS handshake capture can verify presence of server_name under the stated conditions.

requirements.quote:
met.  An endpoint MAY immediately terminate an HTTP/2 connection that
   does not meet these TLS requirements with a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type INADEQUATE_SECURITY.
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 connection does not meet the TLS requirements.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint may immediately terminate the connection with an INADEQUATE_SECURITY connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A noncompliant TLS connection can be presented and its termination and HTTP/2 error type observed.

requirements.quote: A deployment of HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2 MUST disable compression.
requirements.condition: When deploying HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: TLS compression must not be enabled or negotiated.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake configuration and negotiation tests can verify that TLS compression is disabled.

requirements.quote: A deployment of HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2 MUST disable renegotiation.
requirements.condition: When deploying HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2, except for the separately permitted pre-preface credential-protection use.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: TLS renegotiation must not be generally enabled.
requirements.why_checkable: Configuration and runtime tests can determine whether TLS renegotiation is disabled outside the stated exception.

requirements.quote:
endpoint MUST treat a TLS renegotiation as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint encounters a TLS renegotiation that is not within the permitted pre-preface credential-protection exception.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint must treat the renegotiation as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can attempt renegotiation and the resulting HTTP/2 connection error type can be observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MAY use renegotiation to provide confidentiality
   protection for client credentials offered in the handshake, but any
   renegotiation MUST occur prior to sending the connection preface.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint uses renegotiation to protect client credentials offered in the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Any such renegotiation must occur before the connection preface is sent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Such renegotiation must not occur after sending the connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can compare the renegotiation event with transmission of the connection preface.

requirements.quote:
server SHOULD request a client certificate if it sees a renegotiation
   request immediately after establishing a connection.
requirements.condition: When a server sees a renegotiation request immediately after establishing a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should request a client certificate.
requirements.why_checkable: A controlled immediate renegotiation request can verify whether the server requests a client certificate.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST support ephemeral key exchange sizes of at least
   2048 bits for cipher suites that use ephemeral finite field Diffie-
   Hellman (DHE) (Section 8.1.2 of [TLS12]) and 224 bits for cipher
   suites that use ephemeral elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE)
   [RFC8422].
requirements.condition: When cipher suites use ephemeral finite-field Diffie-Hellman (DHE).
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must support ephemeral DHE key exchange sizes of at least 2048 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake tests can offer DHE parameters at the 2048-bit lower bound and verify support.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST support ephemeral key exchange sizes of at least
   2048 bits for cipher suites that use ephemeral finite field Diffie-
   Hellman (DHE) (Section 8.1.2 of [TLS12]) and 224 bits for cipher
   suites that use ephemeral elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE)
   [RFC8422].
requirements.condition: When cipher suites use ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE).
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must support ephemeral ECDHE key exchange sizes of at least 224 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake tests can offer ECDHE parameters at the 224-bit lower bound and verify support.

requirements.quote: [RFC8422].  Clients MUST accept DHE sizes of up to 4096 bits.
requirements.condition: When a client negotiates a DHE cipher suite.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must accept DHE sizes through 4096 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not reject an otherwise acceptable DHE exchange merely because its size is no greater than 4096 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake tests can exercise supported DHE sizes up to and including 4096 bits.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MAY treat negotiation of key sizes smaller than the lower
   limits as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   INADEQUATE_SECURITY.
requirements.condition: When a negotiated ephemeral key size is below the applicable lower limit.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint may treat the negotiation as a connection error of type INADEQUATE_SECURITY.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake using a below-limit key can verify whether the endpoint emits the permitted error.

requirements.quote:
A deployment of HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2 SHOULD NOT use any of the
   prohibited cipher suites listed in Appendix A.
requirements.condition: When deploying HTTP/2 over TLS 1.2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The deployment should not use cipher suites prohibited by Appendix A.
requirements.why_checkable: The prohibited suite list is not supplied in this chunk, so membership and full compliance cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MAY choose to generate a connection error (Section 5.4.1)
   of type INADEQUATE_SECURITY if one of the prohibited cipher suites is
   negotiated.
requirements.condition: When one of the cipher suites prohibited by Appendix A is negotiated.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint may generate a connection error of type INADEQUATE_SECURITY.
requirements.why_checkable: The prohibited suite list is not supplied in this chunk, so the triggering suite set cannot be identified solely from the evidence.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST NOT generate this error in reaction to the
   negotiation of a cipher suite that is not prohibited.
requirements.condition: When a cipher suite that is not prohibited is negotiated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not generate the referenced INADEQUATE_SECURITY connection error in reaction to that negotiation.
requirements.why_checkable: The prohibited suite list is absent from this chunk, so it is unclear which offered suites conclusively satisfy the condition using only supplied evidence.

requirements.quote:
negotiation of a cipher suite that is not prohibited.  Consequently,
   when clients offer a cipher suite that is not prohibited, they have
   to be prepared to use that cipher suite with HTTP/2.
requirements.condition: When a client offers a cipher suite that is not prohibited and that suite is selected.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must be prepared to use the selected cipher suite with HTTP/2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not offer a non-prohibited cipher suite that it cannot use with HTTP/2.
requirements.why_checkable: The prohibited suite list is absent from this chunk, so the complete set of suites to which the checkpoint applies cannot be established from supplied evidence.

requirements.quote:
problem, which causes TLS handshake failures, deployments of HTTP/2
   that use TLS 1.2 MUST support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
   [TLS-ECDHE] with the P-256 elliptic curve [RFC8422].
requirements.condition: When deploying HTTP/2 using TLS 1.2.
requirements.required_behavior: The deployment must support TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 with the P-256 elliptic curve.
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS negotiation test can offer the named cipher suite with P-256 and verify that the deployment supports it.
